validated_results.title: A case--control study of selenium in nails and prostate cancer risk in British men.
validated_results.reason: Population-based case-control study assessing nail selenium concentration and incident prostate cancer risk.

extraction.population: Men under 75 years of age residing in Oxfordshire, West Berkshire, and Leeds

sample_size.excerpt: Out of the 656 study participants, 24 subjects did not provide nail samples (17 cases; seven controls) and five subjects had selenium values that remained very high after repeated laboratory analysis (range 4.6–35.1 p.p.m.) and were thus excluded from subsequent statistical analysis (one case; four controls). In total, 300 case–control pairs were available for analysis.
sample_size.location: RESULTS, paragraph 1; total_n derived from reported group counts 300 + 300 = 600

effect_size.excerpt: Men in the highest quartile had a nonsignificant increased risk compared with men in the lowest quartile (OR 1.24; 95% CI, 0.73–2.10).

confidence_interval.excerpt: Men in the highest quartile had a nonsignificant increased risk compared with men in the lowest quartile (OR 1.24; 95% CI, 0.73–2.10).

comparison.excerpt: Odds ratios for each quartile were calculated using the lowest fourth as the referent category.

design.excerpt: A population-based case–control study of the association between diet and prostate cancer was established in Britain

timing.excerpt: Nail clippings were taken at the time of recruitment and selenium concentration, measured using neutron activation techniques, was successfully assayed for 300 case–control pairs

continent.excerpt: A population-based case–control study of the association between diet and prostate cancer was established in Britain

exposure_measurement.excerpt: The selenium content was assayed using instrumental neutron activation analysis techniques at the University of Missouri-Columbia Research Reactor Center, Columbia, USA.
